blockers: The repo contains ONLY the pretraining pipeline (train.py/train_analysis.py, nanoGPT + hyper-connections) plus an unrelated 'h_and_nu' analysis of the mHC Sinkhorn routing coefficients (analyze/h_and_nu.py). It has NO code for logit lens, attention-head classification (previous-token/induction detection), ablation, path patching, or kurtosis -- the methodology behind every number in the assigned claim. A repo-wide grep for logit_lens/induction/kurtosis/previous_token/attention_sink/top-1 across all .py files returned zero matches.

The post itself (p3/posts/BBgZ4bCbP4dfKeRhk.md) confirms this repo was used only to TRAIN the mHC/mHC-lite/residual checkpoints; the interpretability analysis was performed separately and that code is not published here.

If a replicator instead tried to reproduce the checkpoints from scratch: the mHC variant OOM'd even on a 40GB A100 at the paper-faithful batch size and needed workarounds; full paper-spec training uses ~8x more tokens/iter than what was actually run, and mHC trains ~9x slower than residual (2.76K vs 25.9K tok/s), implying a multi-day single-GPU run just for one checkpoint.
notes: Most surprising finding of this batch: despite the blockers above, all three trained checkpoints (Realmbird/mhc-781m-{residual,mhc,mhc-lite}) are already public and ungated on HF (~1.5GB each in bf16, verified via the HF API), so a replicator would NOT need to redo the expensive multi-day pretraining -- they could download the checkpoints directly and would only need to WRITE the (currently unpublished) TransformerLens-based logit-lens/attention-head analysis themselves, which would then be cheap and would fit a 3090 trivially (781M params). Because that analysis code does not exist in this repo, entrypoint is null per the inspection contract.
